property_summary: For any sequence of calls to Put, the total balance of the contract equals the sum of all msg.value sent; the bug allows reentrant calls to Put during Collect's external call to double-count deposited Ether, breaking the invariant that address(c).balance == sum of all deposits.

After a successful Collect call, the caller's accrued unlockTime is not advanced; the reentrant-collect bug allows nested Put calls before balance deduction, leading to an inconsistent unlockTime for the same balance.

After any sequence of calls to Put and Collect, the sum of all holders' balances equals the sum of all deposits minus the sum of all successful withdrawals; removing reentrancy protection on Put allows a reentrant call during Collect's external call to increment a holder's balance after the deduction, breaking the invariant.

After any sequence of calls, the sum of all holders' balances in Acc equals address(c).balance; removing nonReentrant_ from Put allows a reentrant call during Collect's external transfer to increase the caller's balance after it was deducted, breaking the invariant.

For any sequence of calls starting with a Collect that includes an external call, the contract's invariant that each holder's unlockTime is at most the current block timestamp when their balance is withdrawn remains true; removing the nonReentrant_ guard from Put allows an attacker to re-enter and update unlockTime to a future value while balance is already withdrawn, breaking the invariant.
After any sequence of Put calls, the LockTime of the caller must be at least the block timestamp of the last Put; the bug fails to update LockTime, leaving it lower.
After a Put call, the unlockTime of the caller must be at least the block timestamp of that Put call; the bug fails to update unlockTime, leaving it lower than the block timestamp.

After any call to Put, the caller's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of that call; the mutant drops the unlockTime update, so a subsequent Put may leave unlockTime unchanged from an earlier lower value, violating the invariant.

After two Put calls with decreasing unlock times, a non-zero balance in the second call should be collectable immediately after the second call's block timestamp, which the reference satisfies but the mutant may not due to not updating unlockTime.

After a Put call, if the user's balance is at least MinSum, any subsequent Collect of an amount <= balance in the same transaction must fail because unlockTime was set to at least block.timestamp; the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged, so a Collect can succeed when it should not.

The reference contract must increase the sender's balance by exactly the amount of Ether sent in a Put call; the buggy contract fails to increase the balance, leaving it unchanged after receiving Ether.

After a successful Put call, the contract's Ether balance must equal the sum of all Acc balances; the buggy version violates this by not increasing the sender's Acc balance, so the contract holds more Ether than the sum of balances.

For any sender and value, after a call to Put, the sum of all Acc balances across all addresses must equal the contract's Ether balance; the buggy version fails to increase the sender's Acc balance, so the invariant breaks while the reference holds.

In the reference, a Put call's sender's recorded Acc balance equals the total Ether sent by that sender across all their Put calls (plus any initial balance); the bug never increases it, so for any first Put with a positive value the recorded balance stays zero while total sent is positive.

After any sequence of Put calls, the Ether balance of the contract equals the sum of all Acc balances across all addresses; the buggy version fails to increase Acc balance so the sums eventually diverge.

After any number of Put calls, the locked_ variable inside sGuard must always be false. The mutant modifier, lacking the require(!locked_) guard, allows reentrant Put calls that leave locked_ permanently true.

For any sequence of calls to Put via the fallback, the contract's balance of the attacker must be equal to the total Ether sent, because the reference nonReentrant modifier prevents reentrancy; the buggy modifier allows reentrant calls that credit the attacker's balance multiple times for the same Ether.

After a Put call from a contract that re-enters C during its fallback, the Acc balance of the caller in the reference C equals msg.value sent (reentrancy is blocked, so only one Put is processed), while in the buggy version the balance is greater than msg.value because reentrancy allows the same ether to be credited multiple times.
C's balance must strictly increase after a successful Collect if timestamp equals unlockTime and amount is positive
